decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach to the coin; keep left arm parked and open. Geometry will be refined from wrist views.
Continue bending elbow upward while advancing right wrist toward a downward coin grasp; use modest increments for IK continuity.
Advance toward the holder with continuous wrist rotation; coin remains visible below the open right fingers.
Bring the open right gripper closer to vertical over the coin, preserving the elbow-up branch.
Finish the vertical approach and pause open for visual alignment to the coin edge before closure.
Correct the coin's rightward wrist-image offset with a small lateral translation, descending slightly while starting partial closure.
Coin is centered between the right jaws. Align the edge with a small yaw correction and close fully without translating.
Hold the grasp target closed to allow the fingers to settle before testing retention.
Lift the closed right gripper vertically and verify that the coin separates from the holder and follows the jaws.
Coin is not clearly retained at the fingertips. Reopen and lower above the holder to reassess rather than transport an uncertain grasp.
Pause clear of the loose coin and allow it to settle so a safe recovery grasp can be planned from RGB.
Recover the now-flat coin with an open top-down edge grasp, moving toward its new position while remaining above the table.
Center the flat coin laterally between the open jaws and approach its rim in short downward increments.
Move the jaw center over the coin rim without pressing farther into the table, then begin a slow recovery closure.
Center on the flat coin and lower a few millimeters to engage its edge, then fully close for the recovery grasp.
Recovery descent is obstructed near the holder. Lift clear and change the jaw approach direction to avoid pinching the holder.
Rotate the open overhead grasp to separate the finger sweep from the holder.
Narrow the open jaws above the coin and complete the alternative grasp angle before descending, avoiding the neighboring holder.
Descend with the narrowed jaws clear of the holder, correcting the coin's lateral image offset to approach opposite rim edges.
Avoid deeper table contact; translate the jaw contact line onto the near coin rim and close in place.
Let the rim pinch settle, then make a small test lift while keeping the jaws commanded closed.
Test sustained retention by lifting the pinched rim clear of the tabletop, keeping the gripper fully closed.
The coin remained on the table. Reopen wider than its diameter and return above it for a centered, rather than tangential, recovery pinch.
Translate the open jaw center over the coin face using the wrist image; keep height fixed so the rim is not pushed during alignment.
The coin is now centered at the jaw contact line. Close without further descent while watching for holder interference.
The previous closure appears above the flat coin. Reopen around its diameter and lower carefully to the rim before closing again.
The coin rim appears between both jaws. Keep closure commanded and perform a slow short lift to test this recovery pinch.
The flat coin has slipped beside the holder. Clear the obstructing holder first with a short overhead grasp, keeping the coin on the table.
Correct the wrist-image translation direction and align over the holder to clear the coin's neighboring obstacle.
Align the fingers around the holder's upper edges and close to move it away from the flat coin.
Test lifting the holder clear while keeping the grasp closed; inspect whether the coin remains on the table.
Square the downward approach and align the open jaws around the holder instead of its neighboring coin; avoid an oblique table contact.
Bring the holder top into the jaw contact line with a more vertical approach, then close without further table penetration.
Test the holder pinch and move it slightly toward the robot to separate it from the coin, keeping the grasp closed.
The holder was not retained. Reposition the open vertical gripper over the coin using head-view geometry, staying above contact height.
The flat coin is centered beneath the vertical jaws and clear of the holder. Lower to rim height, then close around its diameter.
Allow the centered diameter pinch to settle, then raise a few millimeters while maintaining full closure to check rim engagement.
Raise the closed diameter pinch gradually and inspect whether the coin remains fixed between the fingertips as the holder recedes.
The coin tipped upright rather than remaining pinched. Recenter on its exposed edge and attempt a narrow side-face pinch at this new orientation.
Reacquire the coin's settled position and approach vertically with jaws wider than its diameter, clear of the holder.
Align the contact point using the wrist view before changing the approach angle to engage the flat coin's rim.
Pivot gently about the coin rim to present the finger pads at a shallow angle, then close while avoiding deeper vertical pressure.
Keep the angled rim pinch closed and lift gently to test retention against the stationary holder.
Reopen and place the coin farther inside the finger pads rather than at their extreme tips, maintaining a shallow approach to the rim.
Bring the coin inside the jaw pads and close slowly without lifting or pressing farther down.
Close completely on the coin inside the pads, settle, and make a small retention-test lift.
The jaws still appear above the coin rim. Reopen and lower the angled pads to engage the coin closer to the tabletop.
Close at the lower rim-contact height and hold still so the coin can settle between the pads before another lift.
Test the lower angled grasp by lifting with full closure, judging retention from the coin's motion relative to the jaws.
The coin is still on the tabletop. Change to a more oblique rim approach so the finger pads can contact its thin edge, keeping the elbow-up configuration.
Lower the oblique open fingers toward the coin rim, with a small lateral centering correction and no arm crossing.
Close the side-approach pinch at the thin rim and make only a tiny lift after settling.
Clear the table and reorient for a top-and-bottom rim pinch, since lateral rim squeezing is ejecting the flat coin.
Continue the wrist reorientation above the table, keeping the arm retracted and on the same elbow-up branch.
Unwind the wrist away from its rotation limit while turning toward a horizontal top-and-bottom coin pinch, remaining clear of the table.
Continue the gradual wrist unwind toward a horizontal coin approach, maintaining clearance and configuration continuity.
Rotate gradually toward a forward-facing gripper with vertical jaw closure, preserving the current elbow-up branch and table clearance.
Continue the wrist rotation toward a horizontal approach while holding the arm position clear of the table.
Finish orienting the gripper horizontally with vertical jaw closure, ready to approach the coin from the near side.
Move toward a near-side rim approach with vertically opening jaws; descend in small increments while monitoring elbow continuity.
